---
title: "Step 2. Select validated images from WIMP"
output: html_document
---

## Purpose

Build a test set of images whose true class a person has confirmed, without
copying anything by hand. The images already sit on WIMP in the source projects;
`select` finds them through the API (read-only) and writes a manifest.

## What counts as validated

The Camtrap DP export has no per-sequence validation flag. A sequence is treated
as validated when either

- its deployment is fully reviewed (`percentInspected >= 99.9` in
  `GET /projects/{id}/deployments/{id}/status`), or
- its observation was made by a person (`classificationMethod = human`).

Sequences with more than one label (two species, or an animal and a person) are
dropped so every image has exactly one true class. Unclassified and
"Animal, unidentified" sequences are dropped.

## Sampling

Up to 250 images per class, round-robin across cameras and then sequences, at most
2 images per sequence while other sequences remain, and no camera supplying more
than 20% of a class unless the class has too few cameras. The seed is fixed in the
config, so the same inputs give the same manifest.

```{python eval=FALSE}
import subprocess
subprocess.run(["python", "-m", "wimpbench", "select", "--config", "config/awt_2026_11.yaml"], check=True)
```

## Output: AWT test set (3 November 2026)

Sources: Skye Anderson's *Wet Tropics Camera Trapping 2025 Skye Cassowary*
projects on PROD (254 deployments, 26 fully reviewed) and TEST (255 deployments,
145 fully reviewed). No image appeared in both. None of Skye's images were used to
train any WildObs model (M. Luskin, 3 Nov 2026).

| Class | Images | Cameras available | In Wet Tropics model |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Blank | 250 | 193 | (detector) |
| Human | 250 | 130 | yes |
| Vehicle | 250 | 49 | (detector) |
| Alectura lathami | 250 | 79 | yes |
| Bos taurus | 250 | 15 | yes |
| Canis lupus familiaris | 212 | 17 | yes |
| Canis lupus dingo | 250 | 85 | no (scored against the model's dog label separately) |
| Casuarius casuarius | 250 | 69 | yes |
| Felis catus | 248 | 24 | yes |
| Heteromyias cinereifrons | 189 | 17 | yes |
| Hypsiprymnodon moschatus | 250 | 50 | yes |
| Megapodius reinwardt | 250 | 87 | yes |
| Orthonyx spaldingii | 190 | 17 | yes |
| Perameles nasuta | 250 | 70 | yes |
| Sus scrofa | 250 | 104 | yes |
| Thylogale stigmatica | 250 | 47 | yes |
| Uromys caudimaculatus | 250 | 63 | yes |
| Wallabia bicolor | 60 | 5 | yes (only 60 validated images exist) |
| Muridae | 250 | 44 | no (common non-target, tests precision) |
| **Total** | **4,399** | | |

"In model" was judged from the labels the Wet Tropics model writes on TEST; the
model's own label list should be confirmed with QCIF.

`results/awt_2026_11/manifest.csv` (public) lists every image by file name and class
only. The full manifest, with source camera, sequence, timestamp, validator and media
link, is kept privately (`state/<set>/manifest_full.csv`, git-ignored; a copy is in the
WildObs Dropbox benchmark folder) because it contains personal names and camera
locations of threatened species. `class_availability.csv` lists every validated label and
how many images exist, for choosing classes in later test sets.

## Known issues

- Dingo and domestic dog: the source projects separate them; the model appears to
  have one dog label. The dingo class therefore shows how dingoes are labelled, and
  a custom match (`Canis lupus dingo` -> `Canis familiaris`) can be applied in
  Colin's evaluation if they should count as correct.
- Small classes (Wallabia 60, Heteromyias 189, Orthonyx 190) give wider
  uncertainty on recall and precision.
